name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

name: bash
description:
Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Git for Windows (MSYS) converts path-looking arguments when invoking native Windows programs: ipconfig /all and cmd /c may break; use ipconfig //all or cmd //c, or a per-command MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL prefix. Exclusions are prefixes: excluding /c also excludes /c/... paths, so use native drive-letter paths for those arguments; do not disable conversion globally. Verify the expected effect as well as the exit code. Output is decoded as UTF-8; native Windows programs may emit OEM/ANSI bytes (for example CP936/GBK) and display garbled text. Use a program UTF-8 option or explicit known-encoding conversion before capture; locale variables alone do not fix native output, and mixed streams cannot safely be guessed or decoded globally as GBK. On Windows, while Experimental native execution / fail-closed (experimentalNative, default ON) is enabled, read-only/workspace-write or unresolved policy is refused before this Git Bash command starts because verified confinement is unavailable. Only an explicitly resolved danger-full-access policy can execute this route. The user can turn off that switch in Settings > Plugins > dsh-gitbash-shell to restore explicitly UNCONFINED legacy Bash, or select danger-full-access in the session access-mode control. Do not switch tools or permissions automatically to bypass a refusal; official file-tool write/edit policy remains separate.
[gitbash tool routing]
Prefer this bash tool for shell syntax, scripts, pipelines, redirection, globbing and POSIX utilities — it is this host's shell.
Fix failed bash syntax in bash; no PowerShell tool is offered here. Do not invent a hidden tool or embed another interpreter as a workaround.
Use gitbash_native before execution when a Windows .exe needs exact literal argv such as /all or /c without MSYS conversion, or independently declared stdout/stderr encodings. Supply an absolute executable, mark each argument literal or path, and select only a known encoding (raw for unknown/mixed bytes). It does not implement shell pipelines, expansion or .cmd/.bat wrappers; only resolved danger-full-access can execute it.
Use gitbash_to_native_path only for a complete caller-declared MSYS filesystem path that a native Node fs/path API needs, especially a runtime-built value. Read native_path from the result. Never convert routes, search strings or shell/program source. Already-native or cwd-relative Node paths need no conversion; ordinary tool path fields already use their own translation. Conversion grants no access.
Choose the execution route before running. A policy/access denial is a stop condition: never switch tools, shells or permissions to bypass it. A decoding/display failure does not mean the command failed to run; preserve its exit facts and never blindly repeat a side-effecting command. Do not guess unknown or mixed encodings.
This bash is Git for Windows (MSYS): paths use drive roots (/c/Users/...), and ~, /tmp, /dev/null and /usr/... resolve exactly as Git Bash resolves them.
[/gitbash tool routing]

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

name: create_goal
description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

name: edit
description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

name: exit_plan_mode
description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

name: get_goal
description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

name: gitbash_native
description: Choose this tool BEFORE execution for a Windows-native .exe that needs exact literal argv (for example /all or /c without MSYS conversion) or explicitly known independent stdout/stderr encodings. Use an offered shell tool instead for pipelines, redirection, globbing, shell expansion or POSIX scripts; this is direct typed argv through the host managed executor, not shell source. Supply an absolute executable, mark literal arguments unchanged and path arguments explicitly; do not put a whole shell command into argv. Prefer a producer UTF-8 option; declare gbk/utf16le only when known, raw for unknown or mixed bytes. In PTC call this offered SDK binding from inside run_code, not as a direct model tool call. Only actual danger-full-access standing policy is supported; missing/restricted policy is rejected before execution. A policy/access denial is a stop condition, never permission for another-tool retry. Decoding/storage failure preserves producer exit: never blindly repeat side effects. No user env, implicit scripts, .cmd/.bat wrappers, path guessing or encoding auto-detection. Known interpreters require explicit entrypoint:interpreter; common CRT/Node argv is supported, arbitrary interpreter quoting is not guaranteed.

description.description: Short description of the intended native operation.

executable.description: Absolute native .exe path. MSYS paths translate only in kind:path values. Bare commands, scripts, .cmd and .bat are unsupported.

argv.description: Each literal is passed unchanged (including /all, /c, quotes and empty strings); each path must be absolute and is explicitly translated to native Windows spelling. No shell expansion.

cwd.description: Absolute typed working directory; omitted means the agent workspace.

entrypoint.description: Default native. Known interpreters require explicit interpreter. Their own command language/quoting is not made safe by direct argv; no automatic script wrapper.

timeoutMs.description: Foreground wait deadline, default 120000ms, capped at 600000ms; expiry promotes the managed process to a job. Not accepted with run_in_background.

run_in_background.description: Use existing managed Jobs; collect with job_output, stop with job_kill. No tool deadline. Requires an attached job controller.

stdoutEncoding.description: Known producer stdout encoding, default utf8. raw preserves unknown/mixed bytes without claiming reliable text. No auto detection.

stderrEncoding.description: Known producer stderr encoding, independently selected; default utf8.

errors.description: Default replace; strict records decoding failures separately from actual command exit. Never rerun a side-effecting command merely because output decoding failed.

name: gitbash_to_native_path
description: Explicitly convert one complete caller-declared path value from the MSYS/Git Bash dialect (/c/-style drive roots, ~, $HOME-style variables, /tmp, /dev/null, Git installation mounts) to its native Windows form and return { native_path }. Call this ONLY when the full value is already known to be a single filesystem path — the tool never inspects surrounding data and never guesses. Pure string conversion through the plugin's shared mount table: no filesystem I/O, no existence check, no permission grant; your runtime policy still governs the converted path. Values that are already Windows-native (drive-letter or UNC) or cwd-relative are returned unchanged, by design. A POSIX-looking value that no mount maps — or whose needed mount fact is unavailable — is REJECTED with an explicit error instead of a misleading passthrough. Independent of the automatic dialect switches; the parameter is named msys_path so the automatic path-field rewrite leaves it untouched. Use it for runtime-built MSYS paths before direct native Node fs/path I/O: await the result and pass result.native_path, never the original MSYS string. Already-native/cwd-relative Node values or ordinary translated tool path fields need no conversion. Never pass routes, search strings, shell commands or program source. In PTC invoke this offered SDK binding from inside run_code. A file policy/access denial is a stop condition, not a reason to convert the spelling and retry through Node or another tool.

msys_path.description: The complete value to convert, as one single MSYS/Git Bash path (drive root /c/, ~, $HOME-style variable, /tmp, /dev/null or a Git install mount). Pass the FULL value only; the tool performs no I/O and no permission grant.

name: github
description: Call the GitHub REST API. The credential stays inside the plugin — it is never returned, and every result is redacted. Write methods require confirm: true.

path.description: API path after https://api.github.com/, e.g. repos/o/r/issues.

name: glob
description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

name: grep
description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

name: hindsight_capture_initiative
description:
Record a new feature or initiative as a tracked knowledge page, so future sessions know it exists and can build on it — and keep that page tracking the plan as it moves.

WHEN TO CALL:
- Starting one: right after the user approves a plan or finishes brainstorming a new feature/capability and you are about to start implementing — BEFORE you write any code. Leave relates_to_page_id empty.
- Plan changed: call it AGAIN — mid-implementation is fine and expected — whenever the goal, scope, or rationale of an initiative you already captured materially changes (an approach is dropped, scope grows or shrinks, the why is rewritten). Pass relates_to_page_id = that initiative's page id so the change lands on the existing page. Never mint a second page for the same initiative.

WHEN TO SKIP: bug fixes, small tweaks, refactors, chores, and trivial course-corrections that leave the goal intact are not initiatives — skip them.

- title: short, specific name (e.g. 'Newsletter refinement chat'). On a recapture, reuse the initiative's existing title.
- summary: 2-3 sentences on what you're building and why — the CURRENT intent, not the originally approved plan (on a recapture, say what changed and why).
- relates_to_page_id: leave empty for a new initiative. Set it to an existing initiative's page id — from hindsight_list_knowledge_pages, or the id this tool returned earlier — to record a plan change or an enhancement to it.

Returns the page id. The page is generated for you — you never format one yourself.

name: hindsight_diagnose
description: Report safe Hindsight runtime diagnostics for this coding-agent session: resolved bank, workspace, harness, config location, API endpoint, and non-secret environment overrides. Use this when memory, hooks, MCP tools, or configuration appear not to work. Tokens and other secret values are never returned.

name: hindsight_ingest_document
description: Save an external document or a block of durable notes/findings into this repository's memory so it informs future recall and pages. Use for design notes, research, or reference material you want remembered — not for the conversation you're already in (that's captured automatically at session end). This is ALSO the correction mechanism: when you verify that a retrieved memory is wrong or outdated, ingest a document titled 'Correction: <topic>' stating what memory claimed, what is actually true, and the evidence — the newer fact supersedes the stale one in future retrieval.

name: hindsight_list_knowledge_pages
description: List this repository's Hindsight knowledge pages — curated, continuously-updated summaries of the project's durable knowledge (architecture, components, conventions, key decisions, and in-flight initiatives). Returns each page's id, title, and a one-line description of what it covers. Call this at the start of any non-trivial task, and again periodically in long sessions, to see what the project already knows before you read code or ask the user. The list changes as work is captured, so re-check it occasionally.

name: hindsight_list_tags
description: List the tags that actually exist in this bank, with how many memories carry each. Use this to DISCOVER families instead of guessing their names: every sibling tool takes a tag as input (hindsight_read_memory_chain expects one 'taken from a recalled memory`s tags'), so a family that never surfaced in a recall is otherwise unreachable. This matters most for per-session story tags (`story:<sessionId>`), whose names are uuids no agent can guess. Measured on a real archive: 21 distinct tags, so the whole list is cheap; pass `prefix` (e.g. 'story:') to narrow it. Combine with hindsight_read_memory_chain to then read a whole family.

prefix.description: only return tags starting with this prefix, e.g. 'story:' (applied client-side; the server ignores its own prefix/ tag/ query params)

limit.description: max rows, as a decimal string (default 200; capped at 1000)

offset.description: rows to skip, as a decimal string (default 0) — the server pages natively

name: hindsight_read_chunk
description: Read the ORIGINAL text a memory was extracted from, by its chunk_id (recall returns one per row). This is the verbatim layer: the memory you were shown is a summary that has already rewritten the wording, so it cannot settle whether it distorted its source — only the chunk can. Reach for this when a memory states a rule, decision, number, or attribution that you are about to rely on, or when two memories conflict and you need to know which one the source actually supports. Note the chunk may contain several messages, including ones the summary dropped entirely.

chunk_id.description: the `chunk_id` of a memory, as returned by recall

name: hindsight_read_knowledge_page
description: Read the full content of one knowledge page by its id (from hindsight_list_knowledge_pages). Call this whenever a listed page is relevant to what you're about to do — e.g. read Conventions before writing new code, Component map before changing a subsystem, or an initiative's page before continuing that feature. A page may contain [[page:<id>]] links to related pages; follow one by calling this tool again with that id. Prefer reading a page over re-deriving the same understanding from source.

name: hindsight_read_memory
description: Read one memory in full by its id, including fields recall does not show (entities, occurred_start/end, document_id, chunk_id, and the raw metadata written at ingest). Use this when the injected memories look incomplete or mutually inconsistent — e.g. two rows describe the same decision with different conclusions, or a row's date is much later than the events it describes. Typically the first step of tracing a chain: read the row you doubt, then follow its chunk_id (hindsight_read_chunk) or its tags (hindsight_read_memory_chain).

memory_id.description: the `id` of a memory, as returned by recall or by this tool's siblings

name: hindsight_read_memory_chain
description: Read every memory sharing a tag, instead of only the handful recall ranked highest. Recall returns at most `rerank_max_candidates` rows (5 by default), chosen by topical similarity — so a row that is part of the same story but worded differently (a later correction, a "this was a test" note, a qualifier recorded in another session) can be excluded no matter how the query is phrased. When a recalled memory carries a tag that looks like a family (`trap:...`, `project:...`, `bank:...`, or any `key:value`), call this with that tag to see the whole family. Measured: 24 rows retrieved where recall returned 5, reaching a decisive row ranked 70th of 106. If you do not know the family's name, hindsight_list_tags lists what exists.

tag.description: a single tag, e.g. 'trap:TRAP-A' — taken from a recalled memory's `tags`

limit.description: max rows, as a decimal string (default 50; capped at 200)

tags_match.description: 'all_strict' (default — only rows that really carry the tag) | 'all' (also return rows with no tags at all) | 'any_strict' | 'any' | 'exact'

name: hindsight_read_source
description: Get the ORIGINAL text behind any memory, automatically following the extra hop that consolidated observations require. Use this instead of hindsight_read_chunk when you do not know whether a row is a raw fact or a merged observation: observations — the layer that carries a project's settled conclusions, and the layer most worth checking — have no chunk_id of their own and point at their source facts instead. This tool walks that hop for you and returns the memory, its source facts, and the first chunk text found. Prefer it when you are checking whether a conclusion is faithful to what was actually recorded.

memory_id.description: the `id` of a memory, as returned by recall or by hindsight_read_memory_chain

name: hindsight_reflect
description: Deep memory reasoning: an agentic synthesis over this repository's FULL memory (git decisions, past sessions, ingested knowledge) that answers WHY questions — the past decision and exact rule/values that explain a behavior, bug, or convention. Slower than hindsight_search_knowledge_pages (several seconds): reach for it when pages are too shallow and you need the root cause or the decided literals. When the answer informs your reply, credit it visibly with a blockquote header: "> 🧠 **From Hindsight memory** — <summary>".

query.description: the question to reason over memory about

name: hindsight_search_knowledge_pages
description: Search this repository's Hindsight knowledge pages for content relevant to a query — hybrid full-text + semantic search, server-side. Call this when the user's question may be answered by the project's accumulated knowledge (architecture, conventions, decisions, initiatives) rather than by reading code. Returns ranked pages with a relevance snippet; read a full page with hindsight_read_knowledge_page. Crediting is mandatory, not a judgement call: if anything these results contribute reaches your reply — quoted, paraphrased, or merely confirming what you were going to say — open that part with "> 🧠 **From Hindsight memory (<page>)** — <the specific facts you drew on>". Rewriting a snippet in your own words does not make it yours. If none of them bear on the turn, ignore them silently — an unhelpful search needs no mention. These are past records: check a claim that something was fixed or works against the code before relying on it.

name: hindsight_sync_status
description: Report whether this repo's memory bank is in sync: gitlog seed present, how much recent history has been deepened with full diffs, conversations ingested, knowledge pages created, and extractions still running. `synced: true` means the seeded memory is fully queryable. Ingestion is automatic and background — if not synced, it is in progress; nothing to run.

name: interrupt_agent
description: Interrupt one teammate's current turn while preserving its pending inbox. Team Lead only.

target.description: Teammate target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents.

name: job_kill
description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

name: job_list
description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

name: job_output
description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

name: list_agents
description: List the Lead and every durable teammate with an addressable target and current availability. inactive means no turn is executing, not a task result. provisioning and failed describe member creation.

name: load_workspace_dependencies
description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

name: present
description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

name: read
description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

name: read_image
description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

name: repo_here
description: Report the GitHub repository of the current working directory (owner/name, default branch, visibility). Read-only.

name: schedule_create
description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

prompt.description: Reminder content to present when the target becomes due.

title.description: Concise task name in the user's language, at most 120 characters. Name only the core action and subject; keep essential target identifiers such as PR numbers and branch names. Do not include execution frequency (e.g. daily, hourly), scheduled dates/times, time zones, task status, or configuration and execution details (e.g. read-only mode, profile-tag filters), even when embedded in the requested or existing title. Do not append parenthetical notes. Put scheduling information in the timing parameters and execution instructions in prompt.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

name: schedule_delete
description: Delete a reminder in the current session, active or inactive. Deletion does not retract a reminder message that is already queued.

name: schedule_list
description: List the active reminders in the current session.

name: schedule_update
description: Change a reminder in place, keeping its id. Supply a new title, prompt, or at most one timing parameter; omitted fields keep their stored values. To change a relative delay, create a new reminder.

title.description: New task name; follow the schedule_create title rules.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

name: send_message
description: Send one message to another Team member. A running target receives it at the nearest step boundary; an inactive target starts or resumes a turn.

target.description: Member target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents, including lead.

name: skill
description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

name: spawn_teammate
description: Create one named, durable teammate. Only the Team Lead may call this tool.

description.description: Short description of the delegated responsibility.

prompt.description: Complete initial task for the teammate.

context.description: fresh starts without Lead history; fork inherits completed Lead turns. Defaults to fresh.

name: subagent
description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

name: subagent_fork
description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

name: team_task_create
description: Create one unowned pending task on the shared Team task board.

description.description: Complete task details and acceptance criteria.

blocked_by.description: Task ids that must complete first.

write_scopes.description: Advisory workspace-relative file or directory prefixes this task expects to modify.

name: team_task_get
description: Read the complete latest value of one shared task before changing or executing it.

name: team_task_list
description: List shared tasks, including readiness, owner, revision, blockers, and write-scope warnings.

owner.description: Optional member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents, matching ownerName; use unowned for tasks without an owner.

limit.description: Number of rows, 1 through 100. Defaults to 50.

name: team_task_update
description: Compare-and-set a shared task action using the latest revision from team_task_get or team_task_list.

name: workflow
description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.
